checks: At the old thresholds and common mass the system is solved since α(0)=0 and F_j(0,b_j)=Q. Its homogeneous linearization gives db_j=−dq/S_j and then −B dq=0. Since each ρ_j and S_j is positive, this proves invertibility for the implicit function theorem.

At each actual mark the positive weighted sum of the through-mark threshold differences from the equalized thresholds is nonnegative by the contact minimum. Some difference is nonnegative, and monotonicity of the smoothed cap mass gives the asserted upper bound on that whole source fiber.
Chain differentiation gives q′=F_t−S_jr_j and q″=K_j−S_jb_j″. Substitution into the twice differentiated contact equation gives the stated sign of the α″ term and denominator B.

K_j is the directional second derivative along the linear threshold path. On a slab of the stated fixed-width form, the threshold distance velocity is r_j/‖u_j‖ and direct differentiation of the primitive gives the cap-loss sign. This description of a slab contribution is local and does not omit other cap terms.

For changing width, differentiating k=s/w gives k′=(s′−kw′)/w. Differentiating the first primitive derivative then gives exactly the square term and both w″ and s″ terms. For w=hΓ_t with Γ_t bounded below and its derivatives and k, Ψ′, s′ bounded, the cross term stays bounded because w′=hΓ_t′. This does not give uniform bounds on all other terms along changing bodies.

The proof needs neither a differentiability theorem for general contact minima nor an implication that the cap is smooth at ramp kinks. The frozen assumptions and conclusion concern one selected source fiber, without asserting a global descent.
